title: Junior Blockchain Developer
description: Entry-level blockchain developer with solid foundational knowledge of blockchain technology, the ability to write and test Solidity smart contracts using OpenZeppelin standards and a development framework (Hardhat or Foundry), basic ERC token implementations (ERC-20, ERC-721), secure handling of known vulnerability patterns, Git-based collaboration workflows, and the ability to build simple dApp frontends connecting to deployed contracts via ethers.js or wagmi.

skills.rationale: A firm grasp of what blockchain is, why decentralization matters, how block structures work, and how transactions flow is the non-negotiable prerequisite for all blockchain development tasks.

Understanding cryptography (hashing, key pairs, ECDSA), wallet mechanics (HD wallets, MetaMask, seed phrases), and basic cryptocurrency economics (gas, ERC-20 vs native coin) is essential for daily blockchain development work.
Writing correct Solidity contracts, implementing ERC standards via OpenZeppelin, writing unit tests, and deploying/verifying on testnets is the core technical output for junior blockchain developers.
Productive use of Hardhat or Foundry, MetaMask for testing, faucets for testnet tokens, and Remix/VS Code for development is required for daily workflow.

Knowing the canonical vulnerability taxonomy (reentrancy, overflow, access control) and using OpenZeppelin's audited libraries defensively is a minimum safety requirement — security failures in smart contracts are irreversible.
Connecting a dApp frontend with ethers.js/wagmi to a deployed contract on Alchemy/Infura, and building ERC-721 NFT projects with IPFS metadata, are common junior deliverables.
Understanding the EVM specification and being able to deploy contracts to major EVM chains (Ethereum, Polygon, BSC) with correct chain ID and RPC configuration.
Basic understanding of Optimistic Rollups (Arbitrum, Optimism) enables juniors to deploy on L2s and understand why gas costs differ from mainnet.
Understanding the oracle problem and why smart contracts cannot access off-chain data is foundational; junior-level Chainlink Data Feed integration is increasingly common.

scoring.description: Each skill score is multiplied by its importance weight. Final score is sum divided by sum of weights.

not_ready.label: Not Ready
not_ready.description: Significant gaps in blockchain fundamentals, Solidity basics, or cannot write a working unit test — not yet ready for production blockchain development tasks.

developing.label: Developing
developing.description: Can write basic Solidity contracts and understands blockchain concepts, but needs guidance on test coverage, security patterns, and deployment workflows.

approaching.label: Approaching Ready
approaching.description: Solid Solidity and Hardhat/Foundry proficiency, writes unit tests, uses OpenZeppelin defensively, and can deploy and verify contracts on testnets with minimal coaching.

ready.label: Ready
ready.description: Meets all junior expectations: independently writes and tests Solidity contracts, implements ERC standards, builds simple dApp frontends, uses Slither in CI, and deploys on EVM chains.

exceeds.label: Exceeds Expectations
exceeds.description: Exceeds junior expectations with early mid-level proficiency: Chainlink oracle integration, L2 deployments, Foundry fuzz tests, or meaningful DeFi protocol interaction.
